subject: History
description: Prithviraj Chauhan, Rana Pratap, Mewar, Rajput-Mughal relations

questions.stem: PRITHVIRAJ CHAUHAN was defeated by Muhammad Ghori at the:
questions.explanation: 1191 — First Tarain: Prithviraj DEFEATED Muhammad Ghori. 1192 — Second Tarain (a year later, Ghori's revenge): Ghori defeated + captured Prithviraj, establishing Turkish rule in N. India. Led to founding of the Delhi Sultanate (Qutb-ud-din Aibak, 1206).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Maharana Pratap fought the famous Battle of HALDIGHATI (1576) against:

options.option_text: Mughal forces under Man Singh (Akbar's general)

questions.explanation: Haldighati — 18 June 1576, fought between Rana Pratap of Mewar and Mughal forces led by Raja Man Singh of Amber + Asaf Khan for Akbar. Mewar held out after the indecisive battle; Pratap conducted guerrilla resistance till his death (1597). Chetak — Pratap's famous horse — died saving him.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The founder of the CHAUHAN dynasty of Sambhar-Ajmer (around 6th-8th century onward) is often identified as:
questions.explanation: Chauhan / Chahamana dynasty — various founders referenced in legendary genealogies. Visaldeva / Vasudeva Chauhan is a commonly-cited name in Bisaldeo Raso/genealogical accounts. Later ruled from Sambhar and Ajmer. Prithviraj III (Rai Pithora) was the most famous — defeated at Second Tarain.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Rajput matrimonial alliance with the Mughals began with which Rajput king marrying his daughter to Akbar?
questions.explanation: Raja Bharmal of Amber — married his daughter (Harkha Bai / Jodha Bai) to Akbar in 1562. Opened up Rajput-Mughal alliance. Their son was Jahangir. Man Singh (Akbar's top Rajput general, Bharmal's grandson) — Amber's famous successor.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The CHITTORGARH FORT — symbol of Rajput valour — is in:
questions.explanation: Chittorgarh Fort — Chittor, Rajasthan. Capital of Mewar before Udaipur. Famous for three jauhars (mass self-immolations of women to avoid capture): Rani Padmini (1303, vs Alauddin Khalji), 1535 (vs Bahadur Shah of Gujarat), 1568 (vs Akbar). UNESCO WHS (Hill Forts of Rajasthan, 2013).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: RANA SANGA of Mewar was defeated by Babur at the Battle of:
questions.explanation: Khanwa — 16 March 1527. Rana Sanga (Rajput confederacy) vs Babur. Babur's second major Indian victory (after Panipat 1526). Ensured Mughal consolidation in N. India. Sanga was wounded and died the next year.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The CAPITAL of Mewar was SHIFTED from Chittor to Udaipur by:
questions.explanation: Udai Singh II — founded Udaipur in 1559 after Chittor fell to Akbar (1568 siege). Udaipur is named after him ('city of Udai'). Rana Pratap succeeded him in 1572. Famous landmarks: City Palace, Lake Pichola, Jag Mandir.
